articles.title: Feasibility, Safety, and Effectiveness of Bleomycin Electrosclerotherapy in Patients with "Giant Hepatic Hemangiomas".
articles.abstract: This retrospective study evaluated the feasibility, safety, and effectiveness of bleomycin electrosclerotherapy (BEST) in nine patients with symptomatic, size-progressive "giant hepatic hemangiomas" unsuitable for surgery. BEST was performed under general anesthesia using six CT-guided needle electrodes. Bleomycin was administered intravenously in three patients and intralesionally in six (3,000-16,430 IU). Follow-up MRI was recommended three months after treatment. Median volume reduction at first follow-up was 18.3% (IQR, 2.7%-36.2%; P = .020) at a median of 77 days (IQR, 44-117 days). Extended follow-up in eight patients demonstrated a median volume reduction of 47.0% (IQR, 17.5%-73.2%; P = .016) at 299 days (IQR, 256-739 days). Six of nine patients reported symptom improvement during follow-up. No major complications occurred; adverse events included three asymptomatic perihepatic hematomas and one intercostal neuralgia requiring prolonged analgesic treatment. BEST was feasible and associated with lesion volume reduction and symptom improvement in this cohort. LEVEL OF EVIDENCE: Level 4, Case Series.

articles.title: Neuropathological findings in 2068 individuals with drug-resistant epilepsy based on updated classification systems: A multicenter retrospective cohort study from China.
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVE: This study was undertaken to investigate the histopathological spectrum of drug-resistant epilepsy (DRE) in a large Chinese surgical cohort using updated World Health Organization (WHO) and International League Against Epilepsy (ILAE) classifications, and to examine its associations with seizure onset age, lesion location, and postoperative seizure outcomes.
METHODS: This retrospective, multicenter cohort study consecutively enrolled individuals who underwent resective epilepsy surgery between January 2011 and December 2020 at three Chinese hospitals. Histopathological diagnoses were updated by two independent neuropathologists based on the 2021 WHO and 2022 ILAE classifications, supplemented by immunohistochemistry and whole exome sequencing when indicated. Postoperative seizure outcome data were collected from medical records and telephone follow-up, with the primary outcome defined as Engel class I at 1, 2, and 5 years after surgery, and Engel class Ia assessed as a secondary outcome.
RESULTS: Of 2099 surgically treated individuals, 2068 with complete data were included. The predominant pathologies were hippocampal sclerosis (HS; 28.4%), epilepsy-related tumors (20.7%), and malformations of cortical development (MCD; 15.4%). Childhood onset epilepsy was associated with MCD and HS, whereas adult onset cases favored non-low-grade epilepsy-related tumors and vascular malformations, with developmental lesions presenting earliest. Whole exome sequencing confirmed mTOR pathway variants in 65.2% of focal cortical dysplasia II cases and SLC35A2 mutations in 62.5% of mild malformation of cortical development with oligodendroglial hyperplasia and epilepsy cases. Among 293 individuals with complete 1-, 2-, and 5-year outcome data (284 included in the adjusted prognostic model), no-lesion cases had significantly lower odds of Engel class I at 5 years than HS (odds ratio [OR] = .21, 95% confidence interval [CI] = .08-.56, p = .002). Temporal lobe location predicted favorable Engel class I outcome (OR = 2.78, 95% CI = 1.31-5.90, p = .008). Engel class Ia results were not statistically significant.
SIGNIFICANCE: Applying the updated WHO and ILAE classifications in this Chinese surgical cohort helps to characterize the pathological spectrum of DRE and may assist in postoperative outcome evaluation.

articles.title: Chronic spinal cord injury in a patient with Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome: Long-term rehabilitation challenges.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Spinal involvement in Klippel-Trenaunay syndrome (KTS) is uncommon, and long-term outcomes after extensive spinal surgery remain poorly characterized.
FINDINGS: A 64-year-old man with KTS developed progressive myelopathy and chronic incomplete thoracic spinal cord injury from an intraspinal vascular lesion causing cord compression. He underwent embolization, decompression, lesion resection, corrective osteotomies, and long-segment fusion. Over subsequent years, neurological and functional decline progressed with bilateral rod fractures, pseudoarthrosis, and sagittal imbalance. Rehabilitation produced modest functional gains without recovery of ambulation.
CONCLUSION: Long-term decline after spinal surgery in KTS may be multifactorial, supporting sustained multidisciplinary follow-up and rehabilitation.

articles.title: Pulmonary vascular complications of hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia.
articles.abstract:
PURPOSE OF REVIEW: The purpose of this study is to present the latest advances and recommendations in the diagnosis and treatment of pulmonary vascular complications associated with hereditary haemorrhagic telangiectasia (HHT): pulmonary arteriovenous malformations (PAVMs), pulmonary arterial hypertension (PAH), pulmonary hypertension associated with high output cardiac failure or liver vascular malformations, haemoptysis, haemothorax and thromboembolic disease.
RECENT FINDINGS: Transthoracic contrast echocardiography has been validated as a screening tool for PAVM in patients with suspected HHT. Advancements in genetic testing support its use in family members at risk as a cost-effective measure. Therapy with bevacizumab in patients with high output cardiac failure and severe liver AVMs showed promising results. PAH tends to be more aggressive in HHT type 2 patients.
SUMMARY: Patients suffering from this elusive disease should be referred to HHT specialized centres to ensure a standardized and timely approach to diagnosis and management.

articles.title: Life-threatening bleeding after tooth extraction due to vascular malformation: a case report and literature review.
articles.abstract: Severe hemorrhages of the oral cavity may be caused by arteriovenous malformations. This case report concerns a 52-year-old healthy female who presented with a painful lower third molar and an extensive arteriovenous high-flow malformation of the floor of the right side of the mouth. During the extraction of the right lower wisdom tooth, an episode of massive life-threatening bleeding occurred. Since the therapy for intraoral arteriovenous malformations of the soft tissue is complex and often difficult to perform, the modus operandi of the present case is presented, and a review of the literature is included.

articles.title: Retrospective evaluation of sirolimus (mTOR blocker) for lymphatic malformations presenting in the neonatal period: a single-center experience.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Lymphatic malformations are rare vascular anomalies. Currently, there is no uniform approach to the treatment of these patients. Neonates with extensive disease often suffer from multiple complications, organ dysfunction, and various tissue lesions, which may be life-threatening and lead to aesthetic deformity. Treatment with sirolimus has the potential to improve symptoms and downsize the lesion, up to complete regression. This retrospective single-center study presents our experience with oral sirolimus in the treatment of newborns with lymphatic malformations, evaluating its efficacy and safety.
METHODS: A retrospective analysis was conducted on 23 patients in the neonatal period and early infancy with lymphatic malformations, treated at the St. Petersburg State Pediatric Medical University between 2021 and 2025. Seven patients underwent primary radical surgical treatment and were not included in the analysis. The final study cohort consisted of 16 patients who received primary conservative therapy with sirolimus. Fifteen out of 16 patients started receiving oral sirolimus before the age of 28 days of life. The median age at the commencement of treatment was 15 days after birth. After instrumental and laboratory examination, sirolimus was administered at a starting reduced dose of 0.5 mg/m2/day divided into two daily doses, followed by a gradual increase under clinical and laboratory monitoring. The therapeutic concentration of sirolimus in the blood (5-15 ng/mL) was monitored once a week.
RESULTS: Disease stabilization or regression was achieved in all 16 patients (100%), with a partial or complete radiological response (≥50% volume reduction) in 13 patients (81.25%) and complete regression (>90% volume reduction) in 10 patients (62.5%) at the 6-month assessment. No treatment-related serious adverse events requiring permanent discontinuation were observed. Recorded adverse events included transient respiratory infections (n = 2), diarrhea (n = 2), aphthous stomatitis (n = 1), and mild anemia (n = 1), all of which resolved with supportive care or temporary dose adjustment.
CONCLUSION: In this selected cohort, sirolimus demonstrated an acceptable safety and efficacy profile, supporting its feasibility as a conservative first-line strategy in neonates with extensive or unresectable lymphatic malformations. However, larger prospective studies are needed to confirm these findings.

articles.title: Promising therapeutic interventions for preserving endothelial glycocalyx integrity in sepsis: a systematic review.
articles.abstract: Endothelial Glycocalyx (eGCX) degradation is a major pathophysiological event in sepsis, contributing to endothelial dysfunction, vascular permeability, inflammation, microvascular thrombosis, and organ failure. Despite its importance, eGCX-targeted therapies are not currently incorporated into standard sepsis management. This systematic review summarized clinical and preclinical evidence on therapeutic and experimental strategies aimed at preserving or restoring eGCX integrity in sepsis. PubMed, Scopus, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, and Google Scholar were searched through August 2026. Eligible human and animal studies evaluated eGCX-directed interventions in sepsis or experimental sepsis models. Outcomes included circulating biomarkers such as syndecan-1, heparan sulfate, and hyaluronan, microcirculatory measures including perfused boundary region, and structural assessment by microscopy. Risk of bias was assessed using RoB 2, SYRCLE, and ROBINS-I. Twenty-one studies were included, comprising 17 animal and 4 human studies. Interventions included ascorbic acid, sulodexide, doxycycline, activated protein C, heparin-based therapies, antithrombin, recombinant thrombomodulin, therapeutic plasma exchange, colivelin, liposomal nanocarriers of preassembled eGCX, and rhamnan sulfate. Several interventions reduced eGCX shedding, improved endothelial barrier or microvascular function, and, in some experimental models, preserved or restored eGCX ultrastructure. Overall, the eGCX represents a promising therapeutic target in sepsis; however, most evidence remains preclinical, and well-designed clinical studies using standardized eGCX outcomes are needed.

articles.title: Tuberculosis-Associated Longitudinally Extensive Transverse Myelitis.
articles.abstract: BACKGROUND Longitudinally extensive transverse myelitis (LETM) involves a continuous inflammatory lesion that spans 3 or more spinal segments. It is a recognized but rare manifestation of Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. CASE REPORT A 51-year-old man originally from Mexico with a significant past medical history presented with altered mental status. He had a 1-year history of a chronic non-productive cough and approximately 20 days of fevers and headaches. Upon admission, he was encephalopathic without neurological deficits, and his Glasgow Coma Scale score was 11. A non-contrast computed tomography (CT) scan of the head was initially negative for pathology. Shortly after admission, he developed respiratory distress and worsening mental status, ultimately requiring intubation. A repeat non-contrast CT scan showed concern for hydrocephalus. An external ventricular drain was inserted into the right lateral ventricle, and cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) samples obtained from the drain were unremarkable. The patient underwent bronchoscopy with bronchoalveolar lavage, and the samples sent for Mycobacterium tuberculosis polymerase chain reaction testing were positive. He remained unresponsive. Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) of the brain and spine was negative for obstruction but revealed diffuse leptomeningeal enhancement across multiple areas, consistent with extensive inflammatory longitudinal transverse myelitis, possibly secondary to pulmonary Mycobacterium tuberculosis infection. Ultimately, the CSF was negative for autoimmune or paraneoplastic processes but showed elevated inflammatory markers. He was treated with high-dose glucocorticoids, plasmapheresis, and anti-tuberculosis therapy. He remained intubated with only moderate improvement and was discharged after 2 months. CONCLUSIONS Tuberculous-associated LETM should be considered in patients with active pulmonary tuberculosis who develop a concomitant inflammatory myelopathy.

articles.title: Case Report: Late-onset BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy with encephalitis, antibody-mediated rejection, and atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome: a rare overlap causing allograft dysfunction, therapeutic challenges, and multidisciplinary management.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Kidney transplantation is the definitive treatment for end-stage renal disease. Late allograft dysfunction has complex and heterogeneous etiologies, and concurrent overlapping pathologies pose substantial clinical challenges that require integrated multidisciplinary management.
CASE PRESENTATION: A 23-year-old female with previously stable allograft function on maintenance immunosuppression presented with progressive clinical deterioration 6 years after deceased-donor kidney transplantation. Initial respiratory symptoms progressed to tonic-clonic seizure, neuropsychiatric disturbances and acute renal function decline. She was diagnosed with active BK polyomavirus viremia with encephalitis, complement-mediated atypical hemolytic uremic syndrome (aHUS), and biopsy-proven BK polyomavirus-associated nephropathy (BKPyVAN) plus concurrent C4d-positive antibody-mediated rejection (AMR). A multidisciplinary team delivered an individualized regimen to resolve the therapeutic conflict: 5 plasma exchange sessions, conversion from mycophenolate mofetil to mizoribine to balance viral control and rejection prophylaxis, plus adjunctive symptomatic therapies. Neuropsychiatric symptoms resolved gradually, and hematological parameters and renal function stabilized by day 29 of admission, leading to a stable discharge. However, the patient progressed to allograft failure and required maintenance dialysis at 1-year follow-up.
CONCLUSIONS: This case highlights the complexity of late allograft complications with overlapping pathologies. Timely multidisciplinary consultation and balanced individualized strategies are critical to optimize clinical outcomes in such rare cases.

articles.title: Efficacy and safety of acute-phase immunotherapy for adult autoimmune encephalitis: a systematic review and network meta-analysis.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Autoimmune encephalitis (AE) is an immune-mediated inflammatory disorder of the central nervous system associated with substantial morbidity. Acute-phase immunotherapy is crucial for improving outcomes, yet the comparative efficacy and safety of available regimens remain unclear. We therefore performed a Bayesian network meta-analysis to compare acute-phase immunotherapeutic strategies for AE.
METHODS: PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to October 2025 for studies evaluating acute-phase immunotherapy in AE. A Bayesian network meta-analysis was conducted. The primary outcome was change in the modified Rankin Scale (mRS) after treatment; adverse events were secondary outcomes. Effects were expressed as mean differences (MD) and risk ratios (RRs) with 95% credible intervals (CrIs). The surface under the cumulative ranking curve (SUCRA) was used to rank interventions.
RESULTS: Eleven studies (1,359 patients) were included, evaluating seven strategies: intravenous methylprednisolone (IVMP), intravenous immunoglobulin (IVIG), IVMP+IVIG, IVMP+plasma exchange (PE), IVMP+IVIG+PE, IVMP+immunoadsorption (IA), and IVMP+efgartigimod (EFG). For efficacy, IVMP+EFG ranked highest in mRS improvement among the included regimens (MD = -0.99, 95% CrI -1.30 to -0.68; SUCRA = 95%), followed by IVMP+IA (MD = -0.87; SUCRA = 88%). IVMP+PE ranked lowest (MD = 0.32; SUCRA = 0.2%). For safety, IVIG monotherapy had the lowest adverse-event risk (RR = 0.51, 95% CrI 0.24 to 0.97), whereas IVMP+PE had the highest risk (RR = 3.10, 95% CrI 0.92 to 9.60).
CONCLUSION: Acute-phase immunotherapy for AE should be individualized by disease severity and antibody subtype. Consistent directional findings were observed in the anti-NMDAR subgroup and, separately, in the subgroup with baseline mRS ≥3. IVMP+EFG and IVMP+IA ranked favorably for short-term functional improvement, although the evidence was based mainly on observational studies and small sample sizes. IVIG remained a reasonable option given its favorable safety profile.
SYSTEMATIC REVIEW REGISTRATION: https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251085606, identifier CRD420251085606.

articles.title: Therapeutic Plasma Exchange in a Pediatric Lupus-Associated Thrombotic Microangiopathy: Prolonged Treatment Guided by Serial Biomarker Response.
articles.abstract: Systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE) is a chronic autoimmune disease involving multiple organs including kidney. Class IV lupus nephritis is the most severe form and sometimes complicated by thrombotic microangiopathy (TMA), leading to microangiopathic hemolytic anemia, thrombocytopenia and acute kidney injury (AKI). We report a 9-year-old female diagnosed with Class IV lupus nephritis complicated by TMA, severe AKI, and resistant hypertension. Therapeutic plasma exchange (TPE) was initiated as an adjunctive therapy due to clinical severity. A total of 15 TPE sessions were performed over 4 weeks. Serial monitoring showed improvement in hematologic parameters, renal function, and clinical status. At 8-month follow-up, the patient maintained clinical and renal remission without relapse. This case highlights the role of prolonged, response-guided TPE in severe lupus-associated TMA in resource-poor settings where complement-targeted therapies are not available.

articles.title: A gastric dieulafoy lesion presenting with life-threatening upper gastrointestinal hemorrhage during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis: a case report.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Dieulafoy lesions are an uncommon but potentially life-threatening cause of non-variceal upper gastrointestinal bleeding, caused by rupture of a large-caliber submucosal artery through a minute mucosal defect; diagnosis is difficult because bleeding is intermittent and the surrounding mucosa appears nearly normal. Hemorrhage from a gastric Dieulafoy lesion during recovery from hypertriglyceridemic acute pancreatitis (HTG-AP) has rarely been reported.
CASE PRESENTATION: A man in his twenties with severe obesity presented with acute epigastric pain after alcohol and a high-fat meal. Serum triglycerides were 53.67 mmol/L (reference 0.56-1.70), and CT confirmed acute pancreatitis. Because of extreme hypertriglyceridemia and evolving organ dysfunction, he received intensive lipid-lowering therapy, plasma exchange, continuous renal replacement therapy, and supportive care in the ICU, and improved. During recovery he developed sudden massive hematemesis with tachycardia, hypotension, and a fall in hemoglobin to 65.9 g/L. Emergency endoscopy showed extensive intragastric clots and could not locate the source. After stabilization, repeat endoscopy revealed an isolated thrombus-like protrusion with active oozing on the lesser curvature near the cardia, with otherwise normal mucosa, consistent with a Dieulafoy lesion; three metallic clips achieved immediate hemostasis. Contrast-enhanced CT excluded pseudoaneurysm, splenic-vein thrombosis, gastric varices, and other pancreatitis-related vascular complications. No recurrence occurred during hospitalization or approximately seven months of follow-up, with healed mucosa on later endoscopy.
CONCLUSION: A gastric Dieulafoy lesion is a rare but life-threatening cause of bleeding during recovery from HTG-AP. A nondiagnostic first endoscopy because of clot retention does not exclude it, and persistent bleeding warrants repeat endoscopy after stabilization and gastric clearance. Bleeding should not be attributed solely to stress injury or anticoagulation; an underlying structural lesion should be sought. Clipping achieved durable hemostasis in this patient, but a single case cannot establish comparative efficacy.

articles.title: [Protective effect of bloodletting at twelve Well-points of hand on neurological function by regulating cortical microglia/macrophage polarization through the IL-10/STAT1 pathway in mice with traumatic brain injury].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To observe whether pricking blood therapy at the twelve Well points of the hand (Well-point bloodletting) can regulate the cortical phenotypic polarization of microglia and macrophages via the interleukin-10 (IL-10)/signal transducer and activator of transcription 1(STAT1) pathway, suppress excessive neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis, and thereby alleviate neurological deficits induced by traumatic brain injury (TBI) in mice.
METHODS: Male C57BL/6 mice were used in the present study which is composed of 3 experiments. The TBI model was established by using an electronically controlled cortical impact device to perform cortical impact. Experiment 1:Twelve mice randomly selected were used as the sham-operation group. Twenty-four TBI mice were randomly and equally divided into a model and a Well-point bloodletting group. Mice in the Well-point bloodletting group received interventions at 6 h, 24 h and 48 h after TBI respectively. The modified neurological severity score (mNSS) and open field test were used to assess the mouse's neurological deficits and locomotor function. Immunofluorescence staining was used to detect the proportions of apoptotic neurons (NeuN+TUNEL+) and microglia (IBA1+) in the injured cerebral cortex tissues. Liquid chip assay was performed to measure the levels of inflammatory factors in the injured cortical tissues, and Western blot was used to detect the expression of cortical STAT1 protein. Experiment 2:The STAT1 agonist 2-NP was applied to activate STAT1 to verify whether STAT1 mediates the anti-inflammatory effect of Well-point bloodletting. Thirty-six TBI mice were randomly and equally divided into model, Well-point bloodletting and Well-point bloodletting+2-NP groups. Mice in the Well-point bloodletting+2-NP group received intraperitoneal injection of 2-NP 1 h before modeling and each bloodletting intervention. The mNSS was used to assess the neurological function, and flow cytometry was utilized to quantify the proportions of M1 microglia and macrophages in the injured cerebral cortex. Experiment 3:this part of the study is conducted to clarify the pivotal role of IL-10 in the anti-inflammatory effect of Well-point bloodletting. The successfully modeled TBI mice were randomly allocated to the model, Well-point bloodletting and Well-point bloodletting+IL-10 antagonist groups, with 10 mice in each group. Mice in the IL-10 antagonist group received injection of IL-10 neutralizing antibody into the lateral ventricle on the contralateral side of the injured cortex 1 h after each bloodletting intervention to block the endogenous IL-10. The neurological deficits were evaluated using mNSS. Western blot was used to detect STAT1 phosphorylation in the brain tissues, and the flow cytometry was applied to measure the proportions of M1 microglia and macrophages in the injured cerebral cortex tissues.
RESULTS: Well-point bloodletting significantly reduced the mNSS scores at 6 h and 48 h (P<0.01, P<0.05) after TBI, down-regulated the proportions of apoptotic neurons and microglia (P<0.05, P<0.01), STAT1 phosphorylation (P<0.05) and IL-2 content (P<0.05), and increased the total travel distance 48 h after TBI (P<0.01) and IL-10 content (P<0.01). Well-point bloodletting+2-NP administration eliminated the effects of bloodletting in down-regulating the mNSS score after TBI (P<0.01) and the proportion of M1 microglia (P<0.01). Well-point bloodletting+IL-10 antagonist administration abolished the effects of Well-point bloodletting in lowering the mNSS score at 6, 24 and 48 h after TBI (P<0.05, P<0.01), suppressing STAT1 phosphorylation (P<0.05) and in reducing the proportions of M1 microglia and M1 macrophages in the injured cerebral cortex (P<0.05).
CONCLUSIONS: Well-point bloodletting can improve the neurological deficits and motor function in TBI mice, which may be related to its functions in inhibiting M1 polarization of microglia and macrophages through the IL-10/STAT1 pathway, and mitigating cortical neuroinflammation and neuronal apoptosis.

articles.title: [Mechanism of electroacupuncture combined with antibiotics targeting dorsal motor nucleus of vagus nerve to activate vagus-adrenal axis, alleviate inflammatory response and reduce mortality in septic mice].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To explore the mechanism by which electroacupuncture (EA) combined with antibiotics regulates the vagus-adrenal axis via the dorsal motor nucleus of vagus (DMV), promotes catecholamine secretion, attenuates inflammatory storm, and improves survival rate in septic mice.
METHODS: Experiment 1:fifty C57BL/6 mice were randomly divided into sham operation group, model group, antibiotic group, EA group, and EA + antibiotic group, with 10 mice in each group. Cecal ligation and puncture (CLP) was performed to establish the sepsis model. Mice in the EA group received 15 min EA (10 Hz, 0.5 mA) at bilateral "Zusanli" (ST36), once daily for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the antibiotic group were intraperitoneally injected with imipenem-cilastatin sodium (30 mg/kg) every 12 h for 3 consecutive days. Mice in the EA+antibiotic group received EA and antibiotic treatment the same as the above. The 3-day survival rate and body weight changes of mice in each group were recorded. ELISA was adopted to detect serum levels of interleukin-6 (IL-6) and tumor necrosis factor-α (TNF-α). HE staining was used to observe pathological changes and the number of inflammatory cells in cecal tissues. Whole-brain optical clearing was performed to detect the expression of proto-oncogene c-Fos protein (c-Fos) in the DMV region. Experiment 2:fifty Chat-Cre mice were randomly assigned to sham operation + empty virus group, model + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group, with 10 mice per group. Corresponding viruses were injected into the DMV 3 weeks before model establishment. CLP operation was conducted 3 weeks after virus injection, followed by daily intraperitoneal injection of clozapine N-oxide (CNO, 3 mg/kg), combined with antibiotics or EA treatment (the same interventions and parameters as Experiment 1). Serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels were measured by ELISA;cecal inflammatory infiltration was evaluated via HE staining. Ultra-high performance liquid chromatography-tandem mass spectrometry (UPLC-MS/MS) was applied to detect serum catecholamines including dopamine (DA), epinephrine (E), norepinephrine (NE), as well as their metabolites 3-methoxytyramine (3-MT), normetanephrine (NMN), and metanephrine (MN) levels. Immunofluorescence staining was used to quantify the counts of forkhead box protein P3 positive / cluster of differentiation 4 positive (FOXP3+/CD4+) cells in cecal tissues.
RESULTS: Experiment 1:compared with the sham operation group, the model group exhibited markedly decreased 3-day survival rate and body weight (P<0.000 1), elevated serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), and increased inflammatory cell infiltration in cecum (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model group, the EA + antibiotic group showed improved survival rate (P<0.05), alleviated body weight loss (P<0.000 1), decreased serum IL-6 and TNF-α levels (P<0.000 1), reduced inflammatory cell infiltration (P<0.000 1), and elevated c-Fos positive cell density in DMV (P<0.000 1). Moreover, all above indicators were superior to those in the single EA or single antibiotic group to varying degrees. Experiment 2:in comparison with the sham operation + empty virus group, the model + empty virus group had higher serum inflammatory factor levels and more cecal inflammatory infiltrates (P<0.0001), and lower levels of catecholamines and their metabolites, as well as fewer FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecal tissues (P<0.000 1). Compared with the model + empty virus group, the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group, and antibiotic + activating virus group displayed reduced serum inflammatory factors and relieved cecal inflammatory infiltration (P<0.000 1, P<0.01, P<0.05), accompanied by increased levels of catecholamines and metabolites, and more FOXP3+/CD4+ cells in cecum (P<0.01, P<0.05, P<0.001, P<0.000 1). Relative to the EA-antibiotic combination + empty virus group, all the above indicators were reversed in the EA-antibiotic combination + inhibitory virus group (P<0.01, P<0.001, P<0.05, except for 3-MT).
CONCLUSIONS: EA at ST36 combined with antibiotics exerts optimal therapeutic effects on CLP-induced septic mice. The underlying mechanism may involve activating cholinergic neurons in DMV, regulating the vagus-adrenal axis to facilitate catecholamine secretion, suppressing excessive inflammatory response, and consequently elevating survival rate.

articles.title: [Comparative study on intervention effects of electroacupuncture at single point "Zusanli" (ST36), "Sanyinjiao" (SP6) and combined points on irritable bowel syndrome mice].
articles.abstract:
OBJECTIVES: To compare the differences in interventional effects among three stimulation modalities:electroacupuncture (EA) at single acupoint "Zusanli" (ST36), single acupoint "Sanyinjiao" (SP6), and their combination (ST36 + SP6), on behavioral and histological outcomes in a mouse model of irritable bowel syndrome (IBS), and to examine the differential neuronal responses in the peripheral and central nervous systems under these modalities, so as to provide experimental evidence for exploring the neural mechanisms underlying acupoint combination stimulation in IBS treatment.
METHODS: An IBS model was established in male C57BL/6J mice by intrarectal instillation of zymosan. The mice were randomly divided into blank control group, model group, ST36 group, SP6 group, and acupoint combination group (n=20 per group except n=18 for the model group). After 7 consecutive days of EA stimulation (2 Hz/100 Hz, 1 mA, 15 min per session, once daily), abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia (referred pain) was assessed using von Frey filaments, motor function by rotarod test, and 3D spontaneous fine behavioral characteristics by an AI-based unsupervised 3D behavioral analysis system. Colon tissue structure and inflammatory levels were observed by HE staining, and colonic inflammatory cytokine expressions were detected by Western blot, to evaluate the symptom-relieving effects of single versus combined acupoint stimulation. For neural tracing, retrograde viral tracers were injected into ST36 and SP6 to label dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons innervating these acupoints in C57BL/6J mice. In vivo two-photon calcium imaging was performed to record DRG neuronal responses to different EA modalities (1 mA, 1 min) in Thy1-GCaMP6s mice, and activity-dependent neuronal labeling was applied using transgenic TRAP2;Ai14 mice to identify central neurons activated by EA (2 Hz/100 Hz, 1 mA, 15 min per session), aiming to reveal peripheral-central neuronal response differences between single and combined acupoint stimulation.
RESULTS: Compared with the blank control group, the model group showed increased abdominal mechanical withdrawal frequency and area under the curve (P<0.001, P<0.05), decreased motor function (latency to fall and rotarod speed at fall, P<0.01), aggravated colonic tissue damage and inflammatory responses (P<0.001), elevated expressions of interleukin-1β (IL-1β) and tumor necrosis factor α (TNF-α, P<0.001), and altered spontaneous behavioral patterns (P<0.001, P<0.01, P<0.05). All three EA modalities significantly alleviated abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia in IBS mice (P<0.001, P<0.05, P<0.01), with the combined stimulation showing a larger effective interventional window than either single acupoint. Compared with single-acupoint stimulation, combined stimulation also more effectively restored colonic tissue damage, reduced TNF-α expression (P<0.05), and shortened the duration of spontaneous arching episodes and altered the transition patterns among different spontaneous behavioral actions (P<0.01, P<0.05). DRG neurons exhibited highly heterogeneous responses to the three stimulation modalities, which could be classified into 3 major categories and 7 subcategories based on their firing characteristics. Furthermore, combined stimulation activated a greater number of DRG neurons than single acupoint stimulation (P<0.05), and the neuronal calcium signal intensity was also higher (P<0.05). Finally, significant differences were observed in the number of responsive neurons across different brain regions under the three modalities. The activated neuronal populations evoked by ST36, SP6, and combined stimulation showed maximal overlap in the paraventricular nucleus of the hypothalamus (PVN), whereas the overlap was minimal in the insular cortex (IC), suggesting that IC neuronal activation requires the synergistic effect of combined acupoint stimulation.
CONCLUSIONS: Combined stimulation at ST36 and SP6 produces superior therapeutic effects over single acupoint stimulation in ameliorating abdominal mechanical hyperalgesia, colonic structural damage, inflammatory status, and spontaneous behavioral changes induced by visceral pain in IBS model mice, and this advantage may arise from the synergistic integration of peripheral and central neuronal responses to different EA signals.

articles.title: β-Asarone Alleviates Post-stroke Neuroinflammation and Improves Mitochondrial Quality Via the BNIP3/BNIP3L-dependent Mitophagy Pathway.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) is a leading cause of death and disability worldwide, with mitophagy playing a central role in post-stroke neurological dysfunction. β-Asarone, a major bioactive component derived from the traditional herb Acorus tatarinowii, possesses antioxidant, anti-inflammatory, and neuroprotective properties. However, whether β-asarone ameliorates IS by regulating mitophagy and its underlying mechanisms remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate whether β-asarone exerts neuroprotective effects against IS by modulating BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy. A middle cerebral artery occlusion (MCAO) rat model and an oxygen-glucose deprivation/reperfusion (OGD/R) cell model were established. Neuroprotective effects were evaluated using neurological behavioral scores, 2,3,5-triphenyltetrazolium chloride (TTC) staining, hematoxylin-eosin (H&E) staining, and Nissl staining. Mitochondrial function was assessed by measuring reactive oxygen species (ROS) levels and mitochondrial membrane potential (MMP). Mitophagy was observed via transmission electron microscopy (TEM) and fluorescence microscopy. Western blot (WB) analysis was performed to detect BNIP3/BNIP3L pathway proteins. Results showed that β-asarone enhanced mitophagy, improved mitochondrial function, and alleviated post-stroke neuroinflammation. Conversely, the autophagy inhibitor 3-methyladenine (3-MA) impaired mitophagic function, exacerbating ischemia-induced brain injury and inflammation, while β-asarone treatment reversed these detrimental effects. In summary, β-asarone mitigates neuroinflammation and neuronal injury after IS, at least partly through promoting BNIP3/BNIP3L-mediated mitophagy, highlighting this pathway as a promising therapeutic target for IS.

articles.title: GNAI2 activating variants and MAGIS syndrome: long-term endocrine and growth outcome.
articles.abstract:
CONTEXT: Germline activating variants in the GNAI2 gene have recently been associated with MAGIS syndrome, characterized by midline malformations of the brain, anterior pituitary gland dysfunction, growth retardation, immunodysregulation, and skeletal defects. However, the full phenotypic spectrum, particularly regarding endocrine dysfunction, remains incompletely defined.
CASE DESCRIPTION: We report on a 9.5-year-old male presenting with MAGIS syndrome due to a de novo GNAI2 (NM_002070.4):c.544A>C, p.(Thr182Pro) variant. He initially presented at 17 months with short stature and hypopituitarism. Pituitary MRI confirmed anterior pituitary hypoplasia with thin stalk and normal posterior pituitary. Long-term follow-up revealed suboptimal response to recombinant growth hormone therapy with persistent low IGF-1, profound prolactin deficiency, and evolving gonadotropin deficiency. He also had delayed developmental milestones, recurrent infections, chronic diarrhea, subclinical hypothyroidism, and skeletal abnormalities. Immunological evaluation showed low T-cell counts, inadequate antibody responses and no overt autoimmune features apart from infantile atopic dermatitis.
CONCLUSIONS: This report details the longitudinal clinical, endocrine, and growth data in a patient with MAGIS syndrome harboring a GNAI2 p.Thr182Pro variant. It highlights the suboptimal growth response to GH with fluctuating height velocity and the development of additional endocrine abnormalities such as prolactin, thyroid dysfunction and suspected gonadotropin deficiency. Detailed phenotypic characterization in such cases is crucial for understanding this complex genetic disorder.

articles.title: Therapeutic-ion-doped bioactive glasses for vital pulp therapy: Linking glass chemistry, release dynamics, immunobiology, and clinical translation.
articles.abstract: Vital pulp therapy (VPT) requires a material to control residual microbial challenge without sustaining injury in a confined, vascularized pulp, while preserving endogenous pulp cells, supporting angiogenesis, and enabling a continuous reparative dentin barrier and durable coronal seal. This critical narrative review asks under what composition-release-exposure conditions therapeutic ion-doped bioactive glasses (BGs) can provide antimicrobial and immune-regulatory effects while preserving pulp cell viability and supporting vascularized reparative dentin formation, and what minimum evidence is required before a formulation can be considered VPT-relevant. Silicate-, phosphate-, and borate/borosilicate-based glasses are compared because network-former and modifier content, processing route, particle size, porosity, and surface chemistry influence dissolution, pH, hydroxycarbonate apatite (HCA) formation, and co-release of Ca, Si, P, and therapeutic ions. Evidence is graded from clinical VPT and in vivo pulp-capping studies through pulp-specific in vitro models to indirect dental and non-dental mechanistic studies. Ag, Zn, Sr, Li, Ce, Ga, and selected emerging Cu- and Co-containing systems are evaluated using a common sequence: material identity and processing; measured release, pH, and interfacial precipitation; microbial and immune response; vascular and dental pulp cell response; and reparative dentin and formulation outcome. Cements, hydrogels, polymer/BG composites, and surface-functionalized systems are considered separately because handling, retention, sealing, and matrix-controlled transport alter exposure. The current evidence is predominantly preclinical and often lacks matched ion release, pH, co-ion, and biological measurements. No dopant can be selected on ion identity alone, and no universal safe concentration can be inferred across glass families or formulations. Clinical progression requires matched material and soluble-ion controls, measured release under biologically relevant conditions, disease-relevant pulp and immune models, formulation-specific handling and sealing tests, and direct safety and reparative-dentin outcomes.

articles.title: Apelin-13 exerts neuroprotection through activation of APJ/mTORC2 axis in microglia after Intracerebral Hemorrhage in mice.
articles.abstract:
BACKGROUND: Apelin-13, a bioactive peptide that acts via the APJ receptor, exhibits potent anti-oxidant, anti-apoptotic, and anti-inflammatory properties. However, its role in intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) remains poorly understood. In this study, we aimed to investigate the therapeutic potential of Apelin-13 and the underlying mechanisms in a mouse model of ICH.
METHODS: A mouse model of intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) was established and randomly allocated to receive either recombinant Apelin-13 (rApelin-13) or phosphate-buffered saline (PBS). To investigate the role of the APJ/mammalian target of rapamycin complex 2 (mTORC2) axis in Apelin-13-mediated neuroprotection, the APJ antagonist ML221 and the mTORC2 inhibitor JR-AB2-011 were administered. To further elucidate the underlying mechanism, microglia-specific knockdown of Rictor was achieved via intracerebroventricular injection of an adeno-associated virus (AAV) carrying CD68-promoter-driven shRictor. Assessments included brain water content, short-term neurobehavioral tests, Western blot analysis, quantitative RT-PCR, and histological staining.
RESULTS: Following ICH induction, the expression of Apelin-13 was upregulated and primarily secreted from neurons. Exogenous administration of rApelin-13 significantly attenuated neuronal apoptosis and improved short-term neurological function in mice after ICH in a dose-dependent manner. Furthermore, rApelin-13 enhanced M2-like polarization of microglia in the post-ICH brain. Notably, the neuroprotective effects of rApelin-13 were abolished by inhibition of mTORC2.

articles.title: Photothermal-responsive Biomimetic Xenon Nanobubbles for Spatiotemporally Targeted Therapy of Ischemic Stroke.
articles.abstract: Ischemic stroke (IS) involves persistent oxidative stress, exacerbated inflammation, and neuronal apoptosis. However, the therapeutic efficacy of current neuroprotective agents is severely restricted by the blood-brain barrier, which hinders their effective delivery to ischemic brain tissue. Although xenon (Xe) exhibits well-documented neuroprotective properties, its rapid diffusion and short in vivo retention limit its ability to match the evolving pathology of stroke. Therefore, developing Xe-based delivery systems with enhanced lesion targeting and controllable release is essential to fully harness the therapeutic potential of Xe for IS. Here, we developed macrophage membrane-coated Xe nanobubbles (Xe-MNBs), namely ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs and IR 820@Xe-MNBs, which respectively carry lipophilic and hydrophilic photosensitizer analogues. Compared with IR 820@Xe-MNBs, ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs exhibited a higher Xe payload, with a measured Xe content of 56.8 μL/mL. Combined in vivo and ex vivo fluorescence imaging demonstrated rapid brain-associated accumulation of the biomimetic nanobubbles within 5 min after intravenous administration. The cranial fluorescence signal of ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs was approximately 3.2-fold higher than that of IR 820@Xe-MNBs, indicating a more pronounced early brain-associated fluorescence signal in the ischemic lesions. Upon near-infrared light irradiation, the photothermal effect triggered nanobubble disruption and Xe release in vitro, enabling externally controlled gas release. Treatment further attenuated oxidative damage and neuronal apoptosis while preserving neuronal integrity in the ischemic brain. Collectively, this work integrated inflammation-associated biomimetic targeting with photothermal-responsive Xe delivery, providing a promising strategy for spatiotemporally regulated gas therapy of IS. STATEMENT OF SIGNIFICANCE: 1. Phorbol 12-myristate 13-acetate (PMA)-induced differentiation of THP-1 cells was employed to construct biomimetic nanobubbles (NBs), endowing them with enhanced adhesion to inflamed endothelial cells and improved targeting of ischemic brain lesions. 2. By integrating fluorescence imaging with photothermal activation, spatiotemporally regulated delivery of xenon (Xe) was achieved, thereby enabling precise therapeutic intervention for ischemic stroke (IS). 3. Compared with the IR 820-based system, ADS 815EI-loaded, macrophage membrane-coated Xe nanobubbles (ADS 815EI@Xe-MNBs) exhibited a higher Xe-loading capacity, greater stability, and more pronounced brain accumulation at early time points, highlighting their potential for therapeutic intervention during the early treatment window after IS.

articles.title: PHLDA3 deficiency attenuates neonatal sepsis-associated acute lung injury and is associated with reduced endoplasmic reticulum stress and NF-κB activation.
articles.abstract: Neonatal sepsis often causes acute lung injury (ALI), but the underlying molecular mechanisms of ALI have not been elucidated. Pleckstrin homology-like domain family A member 3 (PHLDA3) is a stress-responsive protein involved in inflammatory signaling, yet its role in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI has not been explored. Here, we established a neonatal polymicrobial sepsis model via intraperitoneal injection of cecal slurry (CS) and investigated the role of PHLDA3 in ALI using CRISPR/Cas9-generated constitutive PHLDA3 knockout (PHLDA3 KO) mice. CS induced time-dependent upregulation of PHLDA3 in neonatal lung tissues. CS triggered significant increases in the levels of IL-1β, IL-6, and TNF-α in lung tissues, impairing vascular integrity and causing severe alveolar damage. These harmful effects were alleviated by PHLDA3 KO. Transcriptomic analysis revealed enrichment of endoplasmic reticulum (ER) protein processing pathways. CS activated ER stress and unfolded protein response via PERK/eIF2α/ATF4 and ATF6 axes, which were attenuated by PHLDA3 deletion. Pharmacological induction of ER stress by thapsigargin (TG) reversed the protective effects of PHLDA3 KO, whereas ER stress inhibitor 4-phenylbutyric acid (4-PBA) mitigated inflammation and lung injury. In macrophage models, PHLDA3 knockdown was associated with reduced LPS-induced ER-stress-related signaling, NF-κB activation, and inflammatory responses, whereas TG attenuated these effects. Collectively, these findings indicate that constitutive PHLDA3 deficiency is associated with attenuated neonatal sepsis-associated lung injury, reduced ER-stress-related signaling, and decreased NF-κB activation, and support further investigation of PHLDA3 in neonatal sepsis-associated ALI.

articles.title: BCG vaccination mitigates tau pathology and restores cognitive function in PS19 mice.
articles.abstract: Retrospective studies in patients with nonmuscle invasive bladder cancer have reported a significant reduction in Alzheimer's disease incidence (12 to 78%) among Bacille Calmette-Guérin (BCG) recipients versus controls. To investigate the underlying mechanisms, we evaluated BCG in the PS19 mouse model of tauopathy. We found that BCG administration reduced hippocampal phospho-tau and microgliosis while preserving neuronal markers. In vivo volumetric T2-magnetic resonance Imaging (MRI) demonstrated attenuation of brain atrophy accompanied by increased glutamate-weighted chemical exchange saturation transfer-MRI signals. Functionally, BCG-treated mice showed improved performance in the novel object recognition test, as well as improved body-weight maintenance and survival. Transcriptomic profiling of the hippocampus revealed near complete normalization of the PS19 disease-associated gene expression signature toward that of healthy controls. Flow cytometric profiling of brain myeloid populations demonstrated a reduction in activated resident microglia, but total microglia cells remain elevated. Moreover, an increase of trained immunity marker CD80 on the recruited peripheral myeloid cells ensues following BCG treatment. Consistent with this shift in myeloid state, primary brain myeloid cells from BCG-treated mice also exhibited enhanced phagocytosis of fluorescein isothiocyanate-labeled tau fibrils and increased lactate production. Together, these findings indicate that BCG induces systemic and central nervous system myeloid cell reprogramming that limits neuroinflammation, enhances tau clearance, and rescues cognitive and neurodegenerative phenotypes in a tauopathy model. BCG is a safe, readily available therapy that merits consideration as a preventive agent against dementia.

articles.title: Chronic stress activates a hypothalamic vagal circuit to promote hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.
articles.abstract: Hepatocellular carcinoma and depression frequently co-occur, yet the mechanisms linking them remain unclear. Here, we show that chronic stress, systemic inflammation, or neuropathic pain are associated with hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice. Chronic stress hyperactivates a glutamatergic paraventricular hypothalamic nucleus → cholinergic dorsal motor nucleus of the vagus → liver circuit, increasing intratumoral acetylcholine. Single-cell transcriptomics identifies acetylcholine-responsive Chrna9+ epithelial cells that interact with macrophages through COL1A1/2-CD44-STAT3 signaling to promote CXCL1 production. Acetylcholine also promotes tumor cell proliferation through CHRNA9. Circulating CXCL1 crosses the blood-brain barrier and activates hypothalamic glutamatergic neurons, exacerbating depression-like behaviors and establishing a liver-brain feedback loop. Silencing the hypothalamic vagal circuit, tumor-specific Chrna9 knockdown, or systemic CXCL1 neutralization restrains tumor progression and alleviates depression-like behaviors. These findings identify a neural and immune mechanism linking chronic stress to hepatocellular carcinoma progression in male mice.

articles.title: Hydrogen sulfide engages catalytic zinc in HDAC6 to modulate an alternative deacetylation pathway.
articles.abstract: Hydrogen sulfide (H₂S) is a gasotransmitter whose non-covalent effects on protein function remain incompletely understood. Here we show that H₂S-derived sulfur species engage the catalytic Zn²⁺ center of histone deacetylase 6 (HDAC6) and enhance deacetylase activity under defined conditions. Molecular dynamics simulations support access of HS⁻ to the CD2 active-site tunnel, whereas surface plasmon resonance and zinc-depletion experiments support reversible, zinc-dependent engagement. Quantum chemical calculations support a chemically feasible sulfur-associated deacetylation pathway that generates thioacetic acid, which we detect in cell-free reactions, cultured cells, mouse tissues and human serum. Cryo-electron microscopy defines the tandem organization of human HDAC6 catalytic domains and reveals distinct CD1 and CD2 tunnel architectures. HDAC6 loss blunts H₂S-induced endothelial migration and angiogenesis, and CD2 is required for these responses. These findings support HDAC6 as an H₂S-responsive Zn²⁺-dependent deacetylase and link zinc-sulfur coordination to altered deacetylation chemistry.

articles.title: Serine protease inhibitor A3 is a soluble SIRPα ligand that suppresses inflammation and antitumor immunity.
articles.abstract: SIRPα is an inhibitory receptor with the canonical ligand CD47. Here, we show that human serine protease inhibitor A3 (SERPINA3) and its mouse ortholog SERPINA3k function as soluble binders and activators of SIRPα, suppressing SIRPα+ macrophages, neutrophils, dendritic cells and natural killer cells. SERPINA3(k) treatment alleviates lipopolysaccharide-induced pneumonia and ameliorates experimental autoimmune encephalomyelitis and rheumatoid arthritis. Although wild-type SERPINA3 provokes inflammation in cardiomyocytes and brain vascular endothelial cells, the SERPINA3D2 mutant, identified through functional domain mapping for SIRPα interaction, abolishes these adverse effects while retaining full inhibitory capacity. Notably, cancer cells secrete large amounts of SERPINA3(k), exceeding CD47 levels. Anti-SERPINA3(k) antibodies, used alone or in combination with blockade of programmed cell death 1 receptor/programmed cell death ligand 1, inhibit tumor growth in multiple preclinical models. This work identifies a potent soluble SIRPα ligand, offering effective therapeutic strategies for inflammatory/autoimmune diseases and a promising target for cancer immunotherapy.
